method: Sub-component rules OBSERVED in published brand guidelines that document at operational depth. A rule is recorded only where the manual states it explicitly — never where it is implied. This file is a DIFFERENT GRAIN from brand-book-sample.json: that one records which SECTIONS a manual contains, this one records which RULES a section states. The two are not interchangeable and frequencies from one must never be quoted against the other.
why: brand-book-sample.json scored colour.palette identically whether a manual gave one hex or gave hex/RGB/CMYK/Pantone/tints/proportions/pairings/misuse. The product's value is that depth, so the coarse sample was blind to it.

notes.colour.proportions: IRBA states primary 50% / secondary 20% / accent 20% with a per-colour breakdown. Regus states 60% white / 20% black / 10% red / 5% / 5%. Monash mandates a MINIMUM 25% primary across all audiences. None of the three can check adherence.
notes.colour.tints: Commonwealth gives 75/50/25% steps. IRBA states the opposite rule for its primary: 'Tints of the primary colours are not allowed.' Whether tinting is permitted is itself the rule.
notes.colour.dataviz: Monash keeps a separate utility set used ONLY for data visualisation, with an explicit instruction to maintain consistent colour mapping across related visuals.
notes.type.lineheight: Toyota states leading per role: 90% headlines, 110% subheads in print, 145% body. Cedarville states 10pt on 13pt leading for letterhead.
notes.type.alignment: Toyota: 'Flush left, centered or staggered. Never flush right.' Cedarville: hyphenation none.
notes.type.minimums: Toyota distinguishes weight by size and ground: Book for 10pt+ on light, Regular for 10pt- reversed on dark. USWDS sets 16px minimum for body.
